finding.summary: The repaired Kokoro/Piper discriminator is correctly bounded to CPU_FILE_OUTPUT_COMPONENT_ONLY, but its generated WAV bytes are ephemeral benchmark-local data and its first-chunk timing is not a whole FDX request-to-sink latency measurement. A later system-slice run must not compose either field into packet-delivery, heard-output, cancellation-to-silence, or output-start latency credit without a new exact execution binding.
finding.ephemeral_audio: kokoro_piper_cpu_benchmark.py creates each WAV below tempfile.TemporaryDirectory and stores only metadata/hash/sample counts in the JSON receipt. The temporary directory is removed before the receipt is finalized. Therefore a benchmark output_sha256 proves that bytes existed at file-output scope during that execution, but it is not a retained audio artifact that can later be presented as the exact bytes admitted by the FDX packet/sink path.
finding.first_chunk_clock_scope: For both engines, time_to_first_generated_audio_chunk_ms is measured around next(iterator). It is useful as a bounded generator-yield measurement, but it is not by itself a request-admission -> model preprocessing -> first generated sample -> sink admission -> playout-start latency. In particular iterator/synthesize construction and downstream sink timing can sit outside that measured interval.
finding.cancellation_scope: The benchmark drains the producer iterator into audio_parts and then writes a complete WAV. It does not execute FDX3/FDX4 cancellation, post-cancel sink rejection, or packet commit-eligibility. Those invariants remain for the composed owner-VPS system slice.

anti_composition_rules: BENCHMARK_OUTPUT_SHA256 != FDX_SINK_ADMITTED_CHUNK_SHA256 unless the exact bytes are retained and the system execution binds that retained artifact to the existing VoiceOutputPacket lineage.
QUEUED_RUN != EXECUTION and must not be duplicated merely to get a faster answer.
next_execution_contract: Let the existing c711af... runtime dispatch terminalize; classify its exact receipt without scope widening.

If at least one existing engine yields valid real local chunks, instantiate that same pinned engine inside the already-claimed d62224bf... system-slice execution rather than treating the benchmark WAV metadata as the system input artifact.

Start one monotonic request clock at output request admission and separately record model/generator first-yield, first sink-admission and, where representable, virtual-sink consumption timestamps. Preserve each latency as a distinct metric.
Hash each exact generated chunk representation and separately hash/sequence only sink-admitted chunks. Generated-but-discarded post-cancel bytes must stay distinguishable from delivered bytes.

Bind those run-local chunk/sink records to the existing VoiceOutputPacket.packet_id, session/turn/causal lineage and VoiceOutcome. Do not create a second playback state machine or durable voice truth store.

If exact audio bytes need later replay as evidence, persist them only through an already-admitted evidence-artifact mechanism with content hash and retention scope; otherwise preserve hashes/metadata and rerun the pinned producer inside the exact system-slice subject.
next_exact_action: Do not redispatch the queued benchmark. On its terminal receipt, consume only CPU file-output scope. Then execute the existing d62224bf... owner-VPS system slice with fresh run-local chunk-to-packet-to-sink binding and distinct request/generator/sink clocks; only that execution may promote FDX3/FDX4 delivery/cancellation evidence.
